chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged with a judgment that no one before him had judged with, and it was the first judgment he judged with after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). This was when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away and the affair was entrusted to Abu Bakr. A man who had drunk wine was brought to him. Abu Bakr said to him, 'Did you drink wine?' The man said, 'Yes.' He said, 'And why did you drink it when it is prohibited?' He said, 'When I became a Muslim, my house was in the midst of a people who were drinking wine and permitting it, and if I had known that it was forbidden, I would have avoided it.'

Abu Bakr turned to Umar and said, 'What do you say, O Abu Hafs, regarding the matter of this man?' He said, 'It is a dilemma, and Abu al-Hasan (Ali) is right for it.' Abu Bakr said, 'O slave, call Ali for us.' Umar said, 'But he gives judgment in his house.' So they went to him, and with him was Salman al-Farsi.

He informed him of the story of the man, and the man related his own story to him. Ali (peace be upon him) said to Abu Bakr, 'Send someone with him who will go around with him to the gatherings of the Emigrants and the Helpers. Whoever recited the Verse of Prohibition to him, let him testify against him. If no one recited the Verse of Prohibition to him, then there is nothing upon him.'

Abu Bakr did with the man what Ali (peace be upon him) said. No one testified against him, so he freed his way. Salman said to Ali (peace be upon him), 'You have guided them.' Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'I only wanted to renew the emphasis of this Verse among me and among them: Is he who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not guide unless he is guided? So what is the matter with you; how do you judge?'

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: The Helpers (Muslims of Medina who supported the Emigrants)
key_terms.الْمُهَاجِرِينَ: The Emigrants (early Muslims who migrated to Medina)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali rule on a person who drank wine due to ignorance of its prohibition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) judicial acumen in establishing the principle of *jahil* (ignorance) as a valid excuse for exemption from *hadd* punishment, specifically regarding the prohibition of wine. By instructing Abu Bakr to verify if the specific Verse of Prohibition had been recited to the individual, Ali emphasized that legal liability is contingent upon the dissemination of the ruling, thereby reinforcing the Quranic maxim, 'Whoever guides to the truth is more entitled to be followed.' This incident is historically significant as it demonstrates the early application of nuanced jurisprudential reasoning during the transition period after the Prophet’s death.
